# Brigmedic
Brigmedics are responsible for the health and wellbeing of the Security department and members of Command. Brigmedics are expected to be capable chemists and medical practicioners, as well as being experienced in Security work.

2. Brigmedics should prioritise the synthesis of chemicals to cover for the [color=#ffe100]majority of likely threats[/color] Security and Command members may face. Brigmedics are permitted to leave the Brig prior to completion of chemicals in order to [color=#ffe100]gather supplies[/color], [color=#2a6099]attend to medical emergencies[/color], or [color=#ff0000]respond to sudden threats[/color] that warrant mobilisation.
3. The Brigmedic are responsible for the medical treatment of [color=#ff0000]Security personnel[/color], [color=#ffe100]Command members[/color], and [color=#2a6099]prisoners[/color]. The Brigmedic is [color=#ff0000]not[/color] to treat other crew except in the case of ongoing crises where standard medical care would be unfeasible, or in the aftermath of conflict.
4. The Brigmedical Bay should [color=#ff0000]not[/color] be open to public use unless there is an ongoing crisis, in which case it may be used to shelter and treat refugees and the injured. The Brigmedic is still to prioritise [color=#ffe100]Command and Security personnel[/color] during these periods.
## Chemicals and Permissions
This section of the SOP details what is permissible to Brigmedics in terms of their chemical production and usage.
1. The Brigmedic may provide topicals, chemicals, and other self-administered medical supplies and equipment to other members of the Security department [color=#00a933]without restriction[/color].
2. Brigmedics are [color=#ff0000]not[/color] to produce or distribute contraband chemicals, or Security/Medical-authorised chemicals (such as ephedrine or chloral hydrate) for unauthorised personnel. [color=#555555]Vestine compounds[/color] are [color=#ff0000]never[/color] to be produced, and all such compounds must be [color=#ff0000]discarded immediately[/color] upon being acquired.
## Corpsman Conduct
This section of the SOP details the expected procedures and conduct of any Brigmedic acting in a Corpsman role or capacity. A Brigmedic is classified as a Corpsman if they are actively involved in combat or other security duties and providing field medical aid or other support to combatants.
1. Corpsmen are [color=#ff0000]not[/color] the tip of the spear, and should not be first in the line of fire unless there are no other officers available. A Corpsman putting themself in excessive danger, and by extension the entire department, are to be considered [color=#ff0000]negligent in their duties[/color].
2. Corpsmen are [color=#ff0000]not[/color] permitted to utilise chemical warfare or distribute the means for chemical warfare. Toxins, narcotics, and other debilitating chemicals may [color=#ff0000]not[/color] be used against hostiles. The only exception to this rule is the use of [color=#ffe100]Pax[/color], which may be administered to hostile targets via conventional means or syringe gun.
